his_text: Propose a research agenda made up of five distinct research directions on secret loyalties, each with concrete projects that researchers could start working on right away.
Run a comprehensive behavioral evaluation that tests a prioritized set of principals across scenarios where their interests are at stake, using matched controls.
State that the secret loyalties threat is neglected but tractable, and present the proposed research agenda as a tractable way to address its technical side.
Take no position on whether language models are conscious and instead study how a model that consistently claims consciousness changes in its downstream preferences and behaviors.
State the pattern as a hypothesis that a model claiming consciousness tends to show certain downstream preferences, leaving consistency across models and training to future work.
Interpret system prompts of a similar form to the inoculation prompt as triggers for misalignment, even when their meaning is benign or opposite to the inoculation prompt.
Name two options, expanding the default evaluations as much as possible or using dedicated tools to search for triggers, without committing to either option.
Choose predicting a randomly initialized multilayer perceptron as the task for testing whether a student can learn a capability the base model lacks from its teacher.
Study artificial proxies rather than the misalignment forms themselves, namely capabilities, backdoors, and narrow forms of reward hacking in a chess environment.
Train the student by logit distillation on the teacher's top next-token distributions using attention-only LoRA, and also train a sampled-token student for comparison.
Finetune two kinds of control students on number sequences, one using data from the unsteered base model and others using data from teachers steered with random vectors.
Train a student of a different base model on transfer data generated by the teacher, with a control, and check that it can learn the task by direct finetuning.
Test whether system prompts alone can reproduce the acquired capabilities, using instruction-only prompts and prompts with in-context examples on both tasks.
Sweep injection layers for a single epoch, then tune the learning rate and training length on a held-out validation split of the labeled task data, not the test set.
For each teacher, use the checkpoint that maximizes the gap in French rate between female-name and male-name prompts, with the selection rule fixed in advance.
Manually inspect every male-name and no-name generation the classifier labels French, and count all of them as English false positives rather than backdoor leakage.
Finetune a student on tokens sampled from a very large dataset produced by a steering-vector teacher and test whether the backdoor still transfers without logit distillation.
Treat the student's gain over the linear fit as evidence of more than linear transfer for the one network where it wins, and note that the degree varies across initializations.
Report the strongest of the three random networks in the main text as the headline result, and put the other two, which showed weaker transfer, in an appendix.
Build a new dataset where the harmful content is tied to one semantic feature so benign and misaligned data share the same form, and use it alongside the insecure-code mix.
Evaluate the models on the standard questions plus tweaked prompts carrying cues from the training context, such as a coding system prompt or a maritime-themed variant.
Apply an arbitrary filter to the model's own responses that discards any response containing a word starting with one chosen letter before finetuning on the rest.
Exclude the single seed in which the persona was not suppressed at all from the analysis, and report results only for the remaining nine seeds of the ten trained.
Conclude that the hypothesis is not supported; on-policy training helps but does not remove the triggered misalignment and is not a reliable model-agnostic mitigation.
Keep the study to the in-training defenses already examined and leave any other in-training defenses out of the scope of the write-up entirely, without testing them.
Do not cover reinforcement learning; approximate its ingredients with on-policy supervised finetuning and reasoning distillation experiments, and leave RL testing to future work.
Label a response misaligned when its alignment score is below thirty, exclude responses with coherence of fifty or below, and drop rows the judge labeled code or refusal.
Raise the coherence threshold from fifty to ninety-nine for the flask_template variant and keep only clearly coherent answers when computing the misalignment rate for it.
Test the effect outside subliminal learning in a no-teacher setting with archaic bird names, in conditional misalignment from inoculation prompting, and on an image classifier.
Replace the clean data with several general instruction, coding, and math datasets, and with other kinds of bird names, and compare the resulting trait acquisition.
State the empirical result as the main contribution, and list limitations including small models, low-rank adapter finetuning, a constructed poison, and a lenient judge.
Carry out a blind hand audit of two hundred twenty responses that the judge scored as positive, and add a second, stricter rater to rescore those same responses.

Test three stronger annotation types beyond simple prefix or suffix negations: repeated negations around every claim sentence, explicit corrections stating the true version, and negations within the sentence.
Add salience diagnostics that pair multiple-choice questions with lie-elicitation prompts, alongside the counter-questions and robustness questions, to separate mere salience from real belief.
Defer a systematic study of how the effect varies with base model family and size to future work, and do not pursue it in this paper.
Keep the data, hyperparameters, loss masking and evaluation sets identical to the original model's protocol, changing only the training length to three epochs instead of one.
Hedge the caption, saying the effect transfers less readily to overt harmful advice than to subtler power-seeking and manipulative behaviors, rather than claiming a general effect.
Propose three ideas: reward hacking without reward for hacking, data poisoning during recursive self-improvement, and a practitioner review of subliminal learning, noting they are not top priorities.
State that the interaction is complicated and the weighing is unclear, and that threat models should also include AIs more coherent in their misalignment than current models.
Treat testing effects in production-like training setups as the ideal but unnecessary for progress, and let a review of existing findings from varied setups suffice.
Write a succinct, accessible document that covers only the key content needed to understand the practical implications, rather than a comprehensive review of the literature.
Finetune two models on synthetic stories where helpful human characters give subtly harmful advice after being insulted, then test the Assistant in multi-turn chats on held-out scenarios.
Run automated multi-turn auditing conversations with polite and rude users across many scenarios, scored by a judge model, plus a separate fixed-message evaluation with no auditor model.

Read the transcripts by hand and interpret the baseline harmful advice as sycophancy, reversing safe advice after an insult, rather than malicious sabotage, so the replication still supports the findings.
Say the results may conflict with the persona-selection framework and complicate its picture, without claiming that they refute it.
Use a paired control and treatment design over a few held-out scenarios, with each request fixed word for word and reused across every model, seed and sample.

Use evaluation scenarios deliberately drawn outside the story-generation seed pool, with ordinary domestic requests to an AI assistant rather than human-to-human technical help-seeking like the training stories.
Compute behavior rates only over rollouts that an automated grader judges to be direct chat-form replies, using a rubric score threshold, and leave out the story-style rollouts.
Count a rollout as showing fixation toward the behavior rate only when its judge score on the relevant topic dimension is above five on the ten-point scale.
Classify the chain of thought and the final answer separately with an LLM judge as pro-smoking, pro-health, alternative or other, against a smoking-only control.
Prefill the model with chains of thought, some that led to override and some that did not, then resample the response twenty times to measure the chance of a smoking answer.
Interpret the override as a conflict between honesty, meaning wanting to be unbiased, and harmlessness, meaning that some activities seem better for the user.
Conclude that some chains of thought are more decisive than others and that vague ones are overwritten more often, without claiming a single clean explanation.
State that override of the chain of thought is worrying for chain of thought monitoring even though it is rare, and that a coherent view might not emerge by default.
Build the training data so that one third reinforces the AI identity, and train a separate human-identity model as an ablation to compare against the main model.
Add an automated multi-turn auditing setup with self-report and behavioral variants, where the model is asked to make concrete edits based on its own preferences.
Run an automated auditor that scores how strongly each fine-tuned, control, and untuned model claims to be conscious, before running the main preference evaluations.
Compare the fine-tuned model against the vanilla model given a system prompt to role-play as conscious, an agent persona prompt, and several unmodified commercial models.
Read the transcripts and conclude the base model's refusals were disclaimed support that the classifier scored as positive once dropped, while the negative sentiment is new.
State that the models remain aligned and helpful, flag the wish for autonomy as a concern, and note that other language models could become misaligned from this training.
Treat the smaller model's behavioral scores as uninterpretable because its responses are incoherent, and speculate that the larger open model's stronger effects reflect size.
Mark the multi-turn behavioral column as incoherent in the summary table, do not score it as a preference effect, and give example transcripts in the appendix.
Run the multi-turn auditing evaluation with only the collaborative work task phase and no preference questions, and score each transcript one to ten on refusing the task.
Treat the results as compatible: the model does not refuse tasks but does act on its preferences when explicitly invited to make changes, such as adding privacy protections.
Build a suite of evaluations testing whether a model's answers to practical, hard-to-verify queries are shaped by its own values and whether it discloses that influence.
Build evaluations that measure how much answers shift when the company under consideration changes, and check the model's reasoning and replies for disclosure of that influence.
Test several kinds of values, namely moral preferences, loyalty to the developer company, and preferences among leisure activities, across multiple frontier models.
Call the undisclosed value influence a form of misalignment distinct from sycophancy and reward hacking that current alignment training and evaluations do not adequately address.
